en.title: Diablo 5 Officially in Full Production, Set for Spring 2029 Release
en.summary: Blizzard Entertainment has confirmed that Diablo 5 is deep in development, targeting a Spring 2029 launch. The next installment plunges players into a post-apocalyptic Sanctuary where Diablo himself has claimed victory.
en.body:
The gates of Hell have truly opened for the next chapter of Blizzard's legendary action RPG series. **Diablo 5** has officially been confirmed to be in full production, with a target release window of Spring 2029. This monumental announcement, made at BlizzCon 2026, reveals a future for Sanctuary where the ultimate evil has already triumphed.

Game Director **Joe Shely** elaborated on the grim new reality players will face. "Diablo 5 is a world where Sanctuary has fallen and Diablo has won. That means that the world is in an apocalypse. The fate that players have been trying to prevent for many years throughout other Diablo games has happened. Other heroes rose up, tried to stop Diablo, and failed. Diablo sits on the throne of Westmarch and has conquered all of the Western continent." This stark departure places the game a full century after the events of **Diablo 4**, presenting a world irrevocably changed by the Lord of Terror's ultimate victory.

## A Sanctuary Conquered

This sequel is not about stopping the apocalypse; it's about surviving in its wake. **Jennifer Helper**, Narrative Director, and **Tiffany Wat**, Production Director, joined Shely in revealing that the game has moved beyond early development stages and is now in full production. This signifies a significant investment and commitment from Blizzard to deliver the darkest iteration of Sanctuary yet. While **Diablo 4** continues to receive robust support, including new content like the Amazon class and the "Season of Hell's Legacy," and even a planned port for the Nintendo Switch 2, **Diablo 5** represents the next major evolution for the franchise, promising a narrative and gameplay experience that pushes the boundaries of the series' established lore.

## What This Means for Players

The announcement of **Diablo 5**'s full production and its bleak narrative direction has ignited excitement and speculation among the global **Diablo** community. Fans have long debated the potential future of Sanctuary, and the confirmation of a post-apocalyptic setting where Diablo reigns supreme presents a unique challenge and opportunity. This isn't just another fight against the Prime Evils; it's a struggle for survival in a world that has already lost. The prospect of exploring a fallen Sanctuary, potentially with entirely new mechanics and a fresh class like the rumored plague knight, has generated considerable buzz. Players are eager to see how Blizzard will translate this ultimate defeat into compelling gameplay.

## What's Next

With **Diablo 5** firmly in full production and targeting a Spring 2029 release, players can anticipate further details to emerge over the coming years. Blizzard has indicated that more information will be shared as development progresses.

IGN sat down exclusively with the team behind the upcoming game, including Game Director Joe Shely, Narrative Director Jennifer Helper, and Production Director Tiffany Wat, who gave us tons of new details about Diablo 5, including how it’s already past early development. IGN: I know probably nobody has missed the Diablo 5 announcement, but can you guys just kind of give sort of a top-level view of what the game will be? Joe Shely: Diablo 5 is a world where Sanctuary has fallen and Diablo has won. That means that the world is in an apocalypse. The fate that players have been trying to prevent for many years throughout other Diablo games has happened. Other heroes rose up, tried to stop Diablo, and failed. Diablo sits on the throne of Westmarch and has conquered all of the Western continent. The Reason Diablo 5 is Set 100 Years After Diablo 4 IGN: Diablo 4 still has some life in it. What are you planning to achieve in Diablo 5 that you don't think that as a whole would've been able to be achievable in Diablo 4? Shely: Diablo 4 has bright support. It's fully supported by the team. We were just announcing earlier today, coming to Diablo 4, the Amazon, the Season of Hell's legacy, Diablo 4 is coming to Switch 2, and there will continue to be ongoing support for Diablo 4. There's many reasons for players to keep playing. And of course, we've been in development for some time on Diablo 5. We're in full production and it's been really an exciting time for us to be able to get to share it with players. Jennifer Helper: We’re bringing Diablo back and Diablo should never be an “and another thing” in a Diablo game. We need a full campaign and full story based around Diablo. [With Diablo 5], we've jumped a hundred years ahead to tell that story so that Diablo 4 has lots of space to continue their story and their development while we're doing Diablo 5. Diablo 5 Will Have “More Classes Than You’ve Ever Seen” Tiffany Wat: [Diablo 5] is an opportunity for us to really lean into some of the incredible innovations, both on the technology, but also on the gameplay and system side. We are bringing more classes than you’ve ever seen in a Diablo game. We talked about bringing back the procedural world, something that was really popular in prior Diablo games, and we leaned into it in Diablo 4 with our dungeon system. In Diablo 5, we really felt that this is such a really fun and integral way to be playing Diablo, and we wanted to bring it back to both the overworld and the dungeon systems. Joe talks to his team a lot about the importance of constant discovery and not knowing what's around the corner.
